sections.text: The Extreme Value Theorem has one hypothesis: f continuous on a closed interval [a, b]. A break inside, or an open interval, and the theorem gives nothing. Its conclusion is existence: it says a largest and a smallest value occur, not where.

quote.text: f has at least one minimum value and at least one maximum value on [a, b]

problem.text: f is differentiable on [-1, 4], with a relative maximum at x = 1. Must f attain a maximum value on [-1, 4]? Justify.

steps.why: The theorem needs a closed interval.
Yes: by the Extreme Value Theorem f attains a maximum value on [-1, 4].
Not asked; the theorem does not place the maximum.

answer.label: Yes, by the Extreme Value Theorem.

problem.text: g has a jump at x = 2 and a relative minimum at x = 4. Must g attain a minimum value on [0, 6]?

steps.why: The theorem does not apply, so no minimum is assured.

answer.label: No: the Extreme Value Theorem does not apply.
